Our Team
    A new research group building chemical-free, circular solutions for water and soil contamination.
  



  Principal Investigator
  
    
      
    
    
      Dr. Manisha Choudhary
      Assistant Professor
      Carl and Melinda Helwig Department of Biological and Agricultural Engineering · Kansas State University

      
        Dr. Choudhary is an environmental engineer whose work asks a practical and urgent question: how do we build technologies that clean our environment without creating new problems? Her research integrates non-thermal plasma, graphene-based adsorbents, micro/nanobubbles, and circular regeneration strategies for PFAS and other emerging contaminants in water and soil systems.
      
      
        Before launching the EC² Lab at K-State, she held postdoctoral appointments at the University of Maine and Temple University and served as an Assistant Professor in Civil Engineering at Dr. Radhakrishnan Institute of Technology in Jaipur, India. Her work bridges chemical engineering, environmental remediation, science communication, and stakeholder-engaged research.

title: Research
text:
Research Interests
    Chemical-free and circular technologies for emerging contaminant mitigation in the Anthropocene.
  



  
    
      
        
          Emerging contaminants, including PFAS, microplastics, pharmaceuticals, personal care products, and pesticides, threaten drinking water, wastewater, and contaminated soils. The EC² Lab advances physical-chemical treatment technologies that operate without chemical additives, reduce harmful byproducts, and work in complex environmental matrices where conventional approaches often fail.
        
      
    
  

  
    
      NTP
      01
    
    
      Non-Thermal Plasma
      Micro/Nanobubbles
      Wastewater Reclamation
      One Water
      Non-Thermal Plasma-Micro/Nanobubble Reactors for Wastewater Reclamation
      
        Non-thermal plasma can generate oxidative and reductive reactive species capable of degrading persistent contaminants. A major barrier is transferring those reactive species efficiently from the gas phase into water.
      
      
        The proposed EC² Lab approach integrates micro- and nanobubble generators with plasma systems to increase interfacial area, improve mass transfer, and tune chemistry through gas composition, bubble size, and electrical conditions. The lab will use optical emission spectroscopy, high-speed imaging, UPLC/MS/MS, toxicity assays, and qPCR to evaluate treatment performance for PFAS, PPCPs, pesticides, and antimicrobial-resistance concerns.
      
      
        Applications: potable reuse, agricultural irrigation reuse, rural drinking water treatment, and municipal wastewater reclamation.
      
    
  

  
    
      3D
      02
    
    
      3D Printing
      Graphene Adsorbents
      Recoverable Materials
      Soil Remediation
      3D-Printed Recoverable Architected Adsorbents
      
        Nanoadsorbents can offer high contaminant removal capacity, but their small size makes recovery after deployment difficult. Granular activated carbon is practical but can lose performance in the presence of natural organic matter and co-contaminants.
      
      
        This thrust develops 3D-structured porous graphene-based adsorbents using direct ink writing additive manufacturing. Graphene oxide, cellulose nanocrystals, and amine-terminated polylactide will be formulated into printable inks that create recoverable structures for water treatment and in situ soil remediation.
      
      
        Applications: PFAS-contaminated farm soils, agricultural waters, drinking water filtration, and industrial wastewater treatment.
      
    
  

  
    
      RE
      03
    
    
      Circular Economy
      GAC Regeneration
      Microwave Processing
      PFAS Destruction
      Circular Regeneration of PFAS-Laden Adsorbents
      
        Solid-phase PFAS treatment remains a major gap. Thermal regeneration of spent adsorbents is centralized, energy-intensive, can damage adsorbent structure, and may create harmful fluorinated emissions.
      
      
        Building on Dr. Choudhary's work with graphene materials, PFAS-laden granular activated carbon, and plasma treatment, this thrust develops plasma- and microwave-based regeneration methods that act directly on contaminated solid media. The lab will track PFAS release and breakdown, inorganic fluorine, volatile byproducts, pore structure, surface chemistry, and adsorption capacity across repeated cycles.
      
      
        Applications: small water systems, agricultural water treatment, utility-scale adsorbent management, and on-farm PFAS mitigation.

          NTP

title: Join Us
text:
Join the EC² Lab
    We are actively recruiting students and collaborators who want to tackle water and soil contamination with rigorous, practical science.
  



  
    
      
        The EC² Lab is designed to be collaborative, inclusive, and curiosity-driven. We value careful experiments, clear communication, community relevance, and technologies that work outside idealized laboratory conditions.
      
    
  

  Open Positions
  
    PhDPh.D. StudentsActively recruiting doctoral students starting Fall 2026 in non-thermal plasma systems, PFAS destruction, 3D-printed adsorbents, agricultural water reuse, and circular regeneration.Full funding may be available for qualified applicants through research assistantships and project funding.
    MSM.S. StudentsMaster's students can pursue thesis or project-based research in PFAS remediation, water quality analytics, adsorbent characterization, and reactor design.Research assistantships may be available depending on project fit and funding.
    UGUndergraduate ResearchersK-State undergraduates are welcome for independent study credit, paid research opportunities when available, or volunteer research experience.Students from engineering, agriculture, chemistry, environmental science, and related fields are encouraged.
  

  
    
      
        What We Look For
        
          Curiosity and persistence with difficult environmental problems.
          Interest in water treatment, soil remediation, materials, plasma, or analytical chemistry.
          Commitment to inclusive, collaborative research.
          Strong written and oral communication skills.
          Willingness to engage with agricultural and community stakeholders.
        
      
    
    
      
        What We Offer
        
          Hands-on training in advanced environmental treatment technologies.
          Interdisciplinary collaborations across K-State and partner institutions.
          Mentorship shaped by empathy, rigor, and professional development.
          Opportunities to present, publish, and connect research to real communities.
          A new lab culture that students will help build from the beginning.
        
      
    
  

  How to Apply
  
    Prospective students and collaborators are encouraged to reach out before submitting a formal application. Email Dr. Choudhary with the subject line Prospective [PhD/MS/UG] Student - [Your Name] and include:
    
      A brief statement of your research interests and how they align with EC² Lab.
      Your CV or resume.
      Unofficial transcripts, if applying as a student.
      Contact information for 2-3 references, if available.
    
    Email Dr. Choudhary
    For formal graduate applications, visit the K-State Biological and Agricultural Engineering graduate program.

title: Teaching
text:
Teaching & Mentorship
    Empathetic, rigorous engineering education connected to real water and soil challenges.
  



  
    
      
        Teaching Philosophy
        
          As a first-generation graduate, Dr. Choudhary centers empathy, justice, and high expectations in teaching. Her courses combine core engineering fundamentals with active learning, flipped-classroom strategies, laboratory work, and visits to wastewater treatment plants. At the University of Maine, she received over 90% positive student feedback while teaching Wastewater Process Design in Spring 2024 and Spring 2025.
        
      
    
  

  Teaching Experience
  
    
      
        University of Maine
        CIE 434: Wastewater Process Design
        Sole instructor for an undergraduate course with lab in Spring 2024 and Spring 2025.
      
    
    
      
        Guest Lectures
        Water Treatment and Environmental Nanotechnology
        Guest lectures in CIE 430 Water Treatment and CIE 598 Environmental Nanotechnology.
      
    
  

  Planned K-State Course Contributions
  
    UndergraduateENVE 363: Environmental Engineering FundamentalsCore environmental engineering principles, treatment processes, water quality, and sustainability.
    Undergraduate / GraduateCE 565: Water and Wastewater EngineeringEngineering design and analysis of water supply and wastewater treatment systems.
    GraduateCE 762: Water Treatment ProcessesAdvanced treatment technologies for drinking water and persistent contaminants.
    GraduateCE 663: Unit Operations and Processes in Environmental EngineeringMass transfer, reaction kinetics, and process design for environmental treatment systems.
  

  Courses in Development
  
    Environmental NanotechnologyApplications and implications of nanomaterials in water treatment, contaminant removal, and sensing.
    Sustainable Water Reuse and Circular Water SystemsEngineering design for reuse, resource recovery, and One Water approaches.
    Advanced Water Treatment ProcessesNon-thermal plasma, advanced oxidation, membranes, and emerging treatment approaches.
  

  Outreach and Community Engagement
  
    
      
        Learn-by-Doing STEM Experiences
        The EC² Lab plans to develop summer programming for high school students from underrepresented communities, connecting hands-on laboratory experiences to environmental engineering careers.
      
      
        Selected Outreach
        
          Mentored Greely High School students to a Samsung Solve for Tomorrow state championship for PFAS filtration innovation.
          Led Sustainable Engineering Leaders of the Future summer camp sessions for high school girls.
          Served as a Girl Scout water quality workshop instructor.
          Technical volunteer with Water For People.
